subject: Clarify billing units: token quantum, context length, and minimums
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@eunoia.io>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@eunoia.io
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Billing units question — rounding and long-contexts

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Procurement and engineering are trying to map your billing model to our contract and have a couple of concrete asks so we can finish the SOW: 1) how is a ‘token unit’ rounded — do you round per request or aggregate per session? 2) if we send a 25k-token prompt (long context) plus a 1.5k response, how is the charge calculated — is there a minimum slab (e.g., 16k/32k) that triggers a different unit? 3) are there special rules for streaming calls where responses are incremental (partial tokens emitted)?

To make this easier, could you give a sample invoice line for: 3 calls where prompts are 25,000 tokens each and responses are 1,500 tokens each, and one burst of 10 short calls (200 tokens prompt/response) during the same billing window? We need the sample so our finance team can validate the forecast.

Appreciate any worked examples.

—Samira
Procurement Lead, Eunoia Labs
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@eunoia.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing units question — rounding and long-contexts

Hi Samira,

Thanks — great questions. Short answers up top, then a worked example and assumptions.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Rounding: we round per-call to the nearest billing quantum depending on the model SKU. For long-context SKUs we use a 1,024-token quantum for charges; for standard chat SKUs we use a 256-token quantum.
- Minimums: there is a per-call floor for certain committed SKUs (e.g., 16k-slab SKUs have a 16,384-token minimum per call). If a call exceeds the slab threshold we bill the actual rounded-up quanta for the higher slab.
- Streaming: we meter tokens as they are emitted. Partial chunks that don't meet the quantum are rounded up at the end of the call.

Assumptions for the sample invoice below (attached is the same calculation in billing_unit_playbook.xlsx):
- Account is on the 16k-slab committed SKU (per-token rate = $0.0009/token for up to 16,384 tokens, tiered beyond).
- Long-context-capable model uses 1,024-token quantum for rounding. Standard chat uses 256-token quantum.
- For calls >16,384 tokens we move into the ‘over-slab’ pricing band and charge per 1,024-token quantum at over-slab rate $0.00085/token equivalent.

Worked example (3 long calls + 10 short calls):
1) Long call: prompt 25,000 + response 1,500 = 26,500 tokens per call. We evaluate total tokens per call and then apply quantum rounding.
- 26,500 / 1,024 = 25.88 -> round up to 26 quanta (26 * 1,024 = 26,624 tokens charged)
- Billed tokens per call = 26,624. Since this exceeds the 16,384 slab, we apply over-slab rate on the portion above 16,384. For simplicity, we compute effective charge as: (16,384 * $0.0009) + ((26,624 - 16,384) * $0.00085) = $14.7456 + $8.0352 = $22.7808 per long call.
- For 3 such calls: 3 * $22.7808 = $68.3424

2) Burst of 10 short calls: each 200 prompt + 200 response = 400 tokens total. Standard chat quantum = 256 tokens.
- 400 / 256 = 1.5625 -> round up to 2 quanta (2 * 256 = 512 tokens charged)
- Billing: 512 tokens * standard rate $0.0012/token = $0.6144 per short call.
- For 10 calls: 10 * $0.6144 = $6.144

3) Sample invoice line items (rounded to cents):
- Long calls (3): Billed tokens = 79,872 tokens; Line charge = $68.34
- Short calls (10): Billed tokens = 5,120 tokens; Line charge = $6.14
- Subtotal = $74.48
- Applicable tax/fees (estimate) = $6.70
- Total = $81.18

Notes and edge cases:
- If you enable prefix/KV caching, repeated prompt prefixes across calls can reduce billed tokens (we credit reused KV prefix tokens up to the cached window). We'll include sample crediting language in the SOW.
- For streaming incremental responses, we only finalize rounding once the call closes; spikes mid-call don't lead to multiple round-ups.
- If you’d prefer per-session aggregation instead of per-call rounding (to reduce rounding overhead for many tiny calls), we can propose a session-level aggregation (monthly) as part of a pricing concession. That is typically negotiated for high-volume pilots.

I attached a PDF sample invoice (redwood_pricing_sample_invoice.pdf) and the worked spreadsheet. Let us know if you want this presented as a single-line blended SKU for contracting (we can show blended vs split pricing).

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, Samira Khan <samira.khan@eunoia.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-06T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing units question — rounding and long-contexts

Looping in a quick rebuttal / additional clarity on amortization and concessions. Quoting Olga below for context: 

> For calls >16,384 tokens we move into the ‘over-slab’ pricing band and charge per 1,024-token quantum at over-slab rate $0.00085/token equivalent.

Samira — if Eunoia expects persistent long-context calls (e.g., >20k tokens regularly), two pragmatic options reduce invoice unpredictability: 1) a higher committed slab (32k SKU) which reduces per-token overage rate and increases quantum to 2k for that SKU, or 2) session-level amortization where we aggregate all calls within a 24-hour window and apply rounding to the aggregate rather than per-call.

Example of option 2 (session-level amortization) for your exact numbers (3 long calls + 10 short calls aggregated):
- Aggregate tokens = (3 * 26,500) + (10 * 400) = 79,500 + 4,000 = 83,500 tokens
- If we apply the long-context quantum (1,024) to the aggregate: 83,500 / 1,024 = 81.57 -> 82 quanta = 83,968 billed tokens
- Effective billed tokens vs per-call rounding = 83,968 (session) vs 79,872 + 5,120 = 84,992 (per-call) -> session-level reduces rounded overhead by 1,024 tokens in this example, roughly a 1.2% reduction on billed tokens.

If Eunoia would like, we can bake session-level amortization into the pilot contract for the first 90 days as a one-time concession to demonstrate stable invoice behavior.

—Karthik
